newsitem.title: IRAN: India backs gas pipeline from Iran.
newsitem.headline: India backs gas pipeline from Iran.

text.p: Indian External Affairs Minister Inder Kumar Gujral in remarks published on Sunday affirmed India's interest in building a pipeline to transport Iranian natural gas to India.
"He (Gujral)...voiced India's willingness to carry out the establishment of a gas pipeline from Iran to India," the Iranian English-language Kayhan International newspaper reported on Sunday.

Iran and India have been in talks since the early 1990s on plans to construct either overland or undersea pipelines that would link Iranian gas reserves -- the world's second largest -- to the growing Indian market.
But the proposed project is hampered by political, technical and financial challenges, according to industry analysts.
A joint feasibility study on the multi-billion dollar, 2,200 kilometre (1400 mile) pipeline project was stopped by a refusal by Pakistan to allow technical work on its territory.

Iran aims to form an international consortium to build a 1,600 kilometre (1,000 mile) pipeline to Pakistan capable of exporting between eight and 16 billion cubic metres a year of Iranian gas to Pakistan starting in 2002.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since independence in 1947.
